title: Initial summed-counter invariant
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ assign keys to item indices, and let $\mu'$ be an integer-valued memory map. Suppose the cell at address $A.cnt$ contains $0$, and for every key $t<A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)=t$. Then for every $t\le 0$, the cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)<t$, and for every $t<A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)=t$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $t<A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the frequency of key $t$ among indices below $A.n$
replaced:
Let $A$ describe the counter range and let $kf(j)$ be the key of item $j$. If the
counter cell at offset zero contains zero and, for every $t<N_b$, the cell at offset
$t+1$ contains the number of indices among the first $n$ items whose key equals $t$,
then the summed-counter conditions hold at stage zero: the cell at offset zero contains
the number of keys below zero, and for every $t<N_b$, the cell at offset $t+1$ contains
the number of keys equal to $t$.
